simple.meaning: שֶׁבֶר (sheber) is a Hebrew action word meaning “grain (as if broken into kernels).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 9 times in Genesis, Nehemiah, Amos, beginning at Genesis 42:1. The surrounding contexts include family, family line, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שֶׁבֶר (H7668) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: שֶׁבֶר (sheber) / H7668 is traced through Genesis 42:1, Genesis 42:2, Genesis 42:19, Genesis 42:26 with source-language evidence and verse context.

majorEvents.evidenceText: Joseph gathered up all the money that was found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the grain which they bought: and Joseph brought the money into Pharaoh’s house.

timeline.evidenceText: Now Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt, and Jacob said to his sons, “Why do you look at one another?”
He said, “Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there, and buy for us from there, so that we may live, and not die.”
If you are honest men, then let one of your brothers be bound in your prison; but you go, carry grain for the famine of your houses.
They loaded their donkeys with their grain, and departed from there.
When they had eaten up the grain which they had brought out of Egypt, their father said to them, “Go again, buy us a little more food.”
Put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack’s mouth of the youngest, with his grain money.” He did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.
Joseph gathered up all the money that was found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the grain which they bought: and Joseph brought the money into Pharaoh’s house.
Also we made ordinances for ourselves, to charge ourselves yearly with the third part of a shekel* A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces. for the service of the house of our God;
Saying, ‘When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell grain?

definitions.full: H7668. sheber III. שֶׁ֫בֶר noun [masculine] corn, grain , as food stuff (perhaps broken , i.e. thresed , Hoffin ZAW iii (1883), 122 SS Siegf Neh 10:32 ; > Kö ii. 1. 19 n breaking out , i.e. sprouting (as chief fruit of soil); hence Late Hebrew שִׁבָּרוֺן price of corn ); — ׳שׁ absolute Gen 42:1 +; construct 42:19 ; suffix שִׁבְרָם 42:26 , שִׁבְרוֺ 44:2 ; — corn, grain 42:1-2 , 19 , 26 ; 43:2 ; 44:2 ; 47:14 (accusative of congnate meaning with verb), Amos 8:5 (id.); so perhaps (for בָּר ) Gen 42:3 Lag BN 230 ; ׳כָּלשֿׁ Neh 10:32 all kinds of grain .
